jobs.title: Manager, Mobility - APAC
jobs.jd_full:
About Remote

Remote is solving modern organizations’ biggest challenge – navigating global employment compliantly with ease. We make it possible for businesses of all sizes to recruit, pay, and manage international teams. With our core values at heart and future focused work culture, our team works tirelessly on ambitious problems, asynchronously, around the world. You can find Remoters working from 6 different continents (Antarctica left to go!) and all of our positions are fully remote.
With Innovation as one of the core values, we have built Automation and AI capabilities into the requirements for every role.
We encourage every member of the Remote team to bring their talents, experiences and culture to the table to help us build the best-in-class HR platform.
 
If you are energetic, curious, motivated and ambitious, be part of our world. Apply now and define the future of work!

The position

The Mobility team embodies Remote’s dedication to building a worldwide talent community. They ensure employees transition smoothly across borders, adhering to local laws, and provide extensive immigration and relocation assistance. This allows Remote and its clients to secure top global talent, and their commitment to risk management and clear stakeholder communication is commendable. They improve processes for compliance in remote work and business travel, keeping Remote at the global mobility forefront.

Their collaborative approach, combining hands-on immigration management in key markets with strategic vendor partnerships, guarantees seamless transitions for Remote employees, enhancing Remote's global mobility programs and affirming its leadership in the global talent market.

Join Remote at a pivotal time and contribute significantly as a Mobility Manager within our Onboarding and Mobility team. This role offers the unique opportunity to impact the global employment landscape directly.

What you bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing a remote-first, high-volume operational team.
  • A people-first leader that can operate independently and take ownership of the results of the team
  • Proven experience in immigration compliance, global mobility, or similar roles in the immigration space
  • A clear understanding of immigration and typical processes involved in immigration compliance
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment
  • Previous experience in the tech industry or a hyper-growth and scaling environment is ideal
  • Writes and speaks fluent English; additional languages are a plus
  • Experience working remotely is a plus

Key Responsibilities 

People Manager

  • Independently delivers on team objectives with an understanding of how they impact the broader Mobility team and other related teams.
  • Invests time, energy, and enthusiasm in developing self/others to improve performance and gain knowledge in new areas
  • Provides ongoing support and constructive coaching to increase employee effectiveness
  • Creates long and short-term strategies to align with Mobility's vision and goals, including setting targets to meet timelines
  • Reports to Senior Management on metrics, targets, and project alignment
  • Review team budgets and ensure adherence.
  • Oversees the development of relevant processes and procedures to allow prompt and accurate processing and monitoring of immigration and visa applications
  • Manages the preparation of documentation required for new service offerings and organises the training material to roll out for use by other departments
  • Utilizes multiple data sources to analyze and resolve complex issues
  • Has advanced knowledge within a professional area and basic knowledge across all immigration domains
  • Leads projects, delegates, guides and acts as a go-to resource for Mobility Specialists
  • Maintains regular contact with key colleagues and stakeholders using formal and informal opportunities to expand and strengthen relationships
  • Recognizes group interactions and modifies communication styles to suit different situations and audiences
  • Seeks understanding of relevant stakeholders' current and future needs and customizes services to address them better
  • Proactively identifies new ideas/opportunities from multiple immigration sources to improve productivity
  • Uses AI and automation as a natural part of their workflow to drive efficiency and reduce manual effort across immigration operations
  • Views difficult situations and problems as opportunities for improvement

 

Practicals

  • You'll report to: Sr Manager, Mobility
  • Team: Mobility
  • Location: APAC
  • Start date: As soon as possible

Application process

  1. Interview with recruiter
  2. Interview with future manager
  3. Interview with team members 
  4. Bar Raiser Interview
  5. Prior employment verification check 
  6. Offer

Remote's Total Rewards philosophy is to ensure fair, unbiased compensation and fair equity pay along with competitive benefits in all locations in which we operate. We do not agree to or encourage cheap-labor practices and therefore we ensure to pay above in-location rates. We hope to inspire other companies to support global talent-hiring and bring local wealth to developing countries.

At first glance our salary bands seem quite wide - here is some context. At Remote we have international operations and a globally distributed workforce. We use geo ranges to consider geographic pay differentials as part of our global compensation strategy to remain competitive in various markets while we hiring globally.
Our salary ranges are determined by role, level and location, and our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay for the successful candidate in this role is dependent upon many factors such as location, transferable or job-related skills, work experience, relevant training, business needs, and market demands. The base salary range may be subject to change.
At Remote, we foster internal mobility as a key element of our culture of employee growth and development, supported by a compensation philosophy that guarantees pay equity and fairness. Therefore, all compensation changes associated with an internal move will be reviewed by the Total Rewards & People Enablement team on a case by case basis.

The annual salary range for this full-time position is
$48,300—$122,350 USD

Benefits

Our full benefits & perks are explained in our handbook at remote.com/r/benefits. As a global company, each country works differently, but some benefits/perks are for all Remoters:
  • work from anywhere
  • flexible paid time off
  • flexible working hours (we are async)
  • 16 weeks paid parental leave
  • mental health support services
  • stock options
  • learning budget
  • home office budget & IT equipment
  • budget for local in-person social events or co-working spaces

How you’ll plan your day (and life)

We work async at Remote which means you can plan your schedule around your life (and not around meetings). Read more at remote.com/async.

You will be empowered to take ownership and be proactive. When in doubt you will default to action instead of waiting. Your life-work balance is important and you will be encouraged to put yourself and your family first, and fit work around your needs.

If that sounds like something you want, apply now!

How to apply

  1. Please fill out the form below and upload your CV with a PDF format.
  2. We kindly ask you to submit your application and CV in English, as this is the standardised language we use here at Remote.
  3. If you don’t have an up to date CV but you are still interested in talking to us, please feel free to add a copy of your LinkedIn profile instead.

We will ask you to voluntarily tell us your pronouns at interview stage, and you will have the option to answer our anonymous demographic questionnaire when you apply below. As an equal employment opportunity employer it’s important to us that our workforce reflects people of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences and this data will help us to stay accountable. We thank you for providing this data, if you chose to.

Please note we accept applications on an ongoing basis.

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.jd_full:
ABOUT GREYSTAR


Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. Headquartered in Charleston, South Carolina, Greystar manages and operates over $350 billion of real estate in more than 260 markets globally with offices throughout North America, Europe, South America, and the Asia-Pacific region. Greystar is the largest operator of apartments in the United States, managing over one million units/beds globally. Across its platforms, Greystar has nearly $79 billion of assets under management, including over $34 billion of development assets and over $36.5 billion of regulatory assets under management. Greystar was founded by Bob Faith in 1993 to become a provider of world-class service in the rental residential real estate business. To learn more, visit .

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

This position is responsible for developing, implementing, and managing the execution of various specialized projects that support the achievement of multi-faceted organizational objectives. Additional responsibilities may include oversight of budgets, participation in plan development and direct or indirect reporting relationships depending on the project and functional area for which the incumbents reside. Incumbents in this role will partner with colleagues and management internal or external to the department to complete projects that streamline, enhance and/or integrate processes, procedures and actions that result in effective, efficient and/or compliant strategies and tactics.

JOB DESCRIPTION

  • Review and make recommendations on department or cross-departmental planning and design, may contribute in contract negotiations, providing project schedules and budget reporting to regional director.
  • Provide direct or indirect supervision, coordination, and management of all aspects of project work; act as a liaison between different departments, groups and/or 3rd party contacts.
  • May facilitate or directly conduct status report meetings with management team to facilitate communication of schedules and project coordination.
  • Ensure any quality control measures or processes specific to the function are developed, implemented and/or conducted to ensure expectations are met.
  • May create materials, outlines, schedules, procedures and other collateral materials required to effectively manage and execute on projects; may be involved with training or knowledge transfer activities to familiarize and prepare relevant parties for fulfilling any role they may have or impact of the project on them.
  • Partner with other areas and functional groups that may require an understanding of each project.
  • Act as the central point of contact and support for project initiatives engaging other groups as necessary for any additional administrative, functional or programmatic assistance and partnership and managing all phases of communications related to the project.
  • May provide periodic updates and reports for functional groups, stakeholders, business partners, etc. as necessary
  • Create and implement processes and tools for monitoring and project success; Assist in addressing and resolving issues and concerns that arise, as well as seek to provide assistance as needed to ensure a successful experience or ROI.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities:

  • PMP certification preferred or equivalent project management experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to read, write, and communicate effectively to prepare and explain data to team members.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in word processing, spreadsheet, property management (Yardi or One Site), and database management programs in order to complete required reports.
  • Demonstrated mathematical skills necessary to add, subtract, multiply, and divide numbers, decimals, and fractions, and calculate percentages in order to complete financial records, budgets, and other fiscal reporting information.
  • Proficiency in managing multiple timelines and projects simultaneously, setting priorities, and working with little or no direct supervision
  • Project management experience within multifamily industry or relevant functional discipline experience preferred.
  • Able to build and maintain productive and trusting relationships with team members and others with diverse backgrounds and personalities, objectively address and resolve issues, and promote a positive image of the company and its investment strategies and results.
  • Excellent organizational and follow-up skills, ability to set and manage multiple priorities, and oversee detailed project and other intricate plans.

The salary range for this position is $78,000 - $98,000.


Additional Compensation:


Many factors go into determining employee pay within the posted range including business requirements, prior experience, current skills and geographical location.

  • Corporate Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in a quarterly or annual bonus program based on individual and company performance.
  • Onsite Property Positions: In addition to the base salary, this role may be eligible to participate in weekly, monthly, and/or quarterly bonus programs.

Robust Benefits Offered*:

  • Competitive Medical, Dental, Vision, and Disability & Life insurance benefits. Low (free basic) employee Medical costs for employee-only coverage; costs discounted after 3 and 5 years of service.
  • Generous Paid Time off. All new hires start with 15 days of vacation, 4 personal days, 10 sick days, and 11 paid holidays. Plus your birthday off after 1 year of service! Additional vacation accrued with tenure.
  • For onsite team members, onsite housing discount at Greystar-managed communities are available subject to discount and unit availability.
  • 6-Week Paid Sabbatical after 10 years of service (and every 5 years thereafter).
  • 401(k) with Company Match up to 6% of pay after 6 months of service.
  • Paid Parental Leave and lifetime Fertility Benefit reimbursement up to $10,000 (includes adoption or surrogacy).
  • Employee Assistance Program.
  • Critical Illness, Accident, Hospital Indemnity, Pet Insurance and Legal Plans.
  • Charitable giving program and benefits.

*Benefits offered for full-time employees. For Union and Prevailing Wage roles, compensation and benefits may vary from the listed information above due to Collective Bargaining Agreements and/or local governing authority.


Greystar will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.


Greystar is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.


This position may be performed remotely anywhere within the United States except the state of Alaska.


Important Notice: Greystar will never request your banking details or other sensitive personal information during the interview process. Greystar does not conduct any interviews via text or messaging, and all communication will come from official Greystar email addresses (@greystar.com). If you receive suspicious requests, please report them immediately to .


ANTICIPATED CLOSING DATE

October 10, 2026

This date may be subject to change due to evolving business needs.

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.jd_full:
About Darkroom

Darkroom is the leading next-generation growth marketing firm engineering the brands of tomorrow. Founded in 2017, we set out to redefine what a modern agency could be, by replacing the inertia of legacy advertising behemoths with a model built for speed, intelligence, and measurable impact.

At our core, Darkroom is a human services company powered by Shadow, a universal AI commerce layer that integrates executive-level strategy with proprietary agentic technology. This fusion enables our teams to deliver outsized returns by enhancing creative output, operational efficiency, and revenue generation across every stage of the customer journey.

Our track record speaks for itself: billions in attributable revenue driven across e-commerce marketplaces, media networks, DTC ecosystems, and social commerce platforms. Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom’s role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.

About the Role

This is a dedicated role on a single account, helping a key client bring a brand new product to market, with Darkroom owning all media channels. You are the operational owner of that engagement: the person accountable for the program running on time, in scope, and against every commitment, with no slips in timeline.

That makes this different from a typical agency PM job. You are not coordinating a portfolio. You are going deep on one enterprise client, holding the operating rhythm, and creating accountability within the layers of Darkroom.

You will report to the Director of Growth Strategy on the Hark engagement, with a dotted line to the Managing Director, Paid Media. You will work daily with Paid Social and Paid Search Specialists, Analytics, Creative, and the client’s own program leads.

This is a fully remote role supporting a team in the EST time zone (9 AM–5 PM EST).

What You’ll Do

  • Service level accountability. You track our contracted SLAs, produce the reporting that evidences adherence, and escalate early when something is trending toward a miss. When the client asks whether we hit our commitments, the answer comes from you and it is already documented.

  • The Shared Model. You maintain Darkroom’s side of the jointly held media plan, forecast, and ramp model, keep it reconciled against actuals, and manage the cadence with the client’s team so both sides are always working off the same numbers.

  • Scope and budget control. You own hours tracking, scope-versus-delivered reconciliation, and ensuring we stay within scope.

  • The operating rhythm. Standups, client status calls, internal syncs, QBR prep. Decisions, action items, and blockers documented and visible to both sides.

  • Cross-functional handoffs. Briefs, assets, performance reporting, and campaign builds moving between Media, Creative, and Analytics on schedule, with dependencies mapped.

  • Resourcing and capacity. Working with the Director of Growth Strategy and team leads to keep staffing matched to the work, and surfacing capacity risk before it shows up as a slipped deadline.

  • Risk escalation. You are the point of escalation for cross-team dependencies and you keep stakeholders aligned without routing every conversation through leadership.

You Should Apply If This Sounds Like You

  • You have 3-5+ years of project or program management experience, ideally at a media, marketing, creative, or digital agency

  • You’re conversant in paid media workflows and terminology: campaign builds, flight dates, creative rotations, reporting cadences, even if you’ve never bought media yourself

  • You build the tracker before someone asks for it, and you notice when a timeline is about to slip before anyone else does

  • You’re a clear, proactive communicator, comfortable managing up, across, and with clients when needed

  • You are a Notion guru. Notion is Darkroom’s spine, and one needs to be fluent in Notion. This means designing and maintaining relational databases, building filtered views, and maintaining SOPs.

  • You’re comfortable working across Slack, Toggl, and Google Sheets-based trackers as your daily toolkit

  • You can juggle multiple accounts and shifting priorities without dropping details

  • You hold a high bar for your own output and expect the same from the people you coordinate with

What It’s Like to Work at Darkroom

Darkroom is not a typical agency. We are looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect every team member to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership — but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape — just world-class talent building something remarkable.

We believe in autonomy with accountability, truth over comfort, and outcomes over optics.

  • Unlimited PTO + Local holidays (Relevant to your hub): Rebooting is part of the work. Take the time you need to stay sharp.

  • Remote-First Culture: Many roles are fully remote. Employees based in or near our New York or Lisbon HQs are expected to work hybrid with weekly in-office time. Hub locations include the Brazil and Spain.

  • Parental Leave: Flexible parental leave to support new parents during this important transition.

  • Growth: Our interdisciplinary model gives every Darkroomer exposure far beyond their core role. Grow your skills, expand your influence, and stay at the forefront of the industry.

Equal Opportunity Statement

Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace—we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national orientation, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

jobs.title: Product Manager - Lansa
jobs.jd_full:
We are looking for a motivated, energetic Product Manager to join the LANSA team.

LANSA has a 30-year track record of enabling customers to magnify the ROI of their IT spend. While most other development and integration tools have come and gone over the years, our customers have easily transitioned their applications into new technologies. LANSA’s flagship offering is Visual LANSA, the original low-code, rapid application development platform for professional mobile, web, and cloud developers. It provides a single-language IDE to generate the client-side, server-side, and everything in-between.

Idera brands, including LANSA, are utilized world-wide by many Fortune 100, Fortune 500 and small businesses. We have more than 50K customers worldwide including some of the world’s largest healthcare, financial services, retail and technology companies. At Idera you will have an opportunity to grow your product and leadership skills in a fun, rapid pace and innovative work environment.

Responsibilities:

  • Drive the direction, feature set and release cadence for LANSA
  • Work with customers, internal stakeholders and remote development teams to drive product feature definition
  • Plan and facilitate conversations across our organizations to understand requirements and pain points and devise simple solutions to address those
  • Document future product features and requirements into well-organized detailed written product requirements
  • Drive and track product development progress with various development teams
  • Communicate product roadmap and product value propositions to marketing and sales teams
  • See yourself as a problem solver, able to think creatively to remove obstacles
  • You prefer to be hands-on with your products, able to install and use what your target users use, putting yourself in their shoes
  • You will interact with all levels and departments of a major software company - so your ability to communicate and influence others will be a key to your success
  • Organize and prioritize product features and enhancements to align with business goals and customer needs.
  • Manage well projects end-to-end from inception to launch, coordinating successful product releases and facilitating post-launch support, including webinars in collaboration with Clients, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Support and other related teams.
  • Leverage technical understanding to collaborate effectively with Engineering, contributing to solution brainstorming and technical discussions.

Must-have Qualifications

  • Previous product management or equivalent experience
  •  Excellent problem solving capabilities, unanswered riddles drive you crazy
  • Ability to influence without authority, establish rapport and demonstrate confidence with your product vision
  • Experience working with international teams that cross multiple time zones and with large organizations
  • Ability to communicate professionally with executive leadership
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and queries from team members simultaneously
  •  Ability to be flexible and embrace change
  •  Ability to quickly pick up technical concepts and terminology
  • Independent, proactive and detailed to resolve issues and drive impactful product growth

Important but not absolute must-have Qualifications

  • Familiarity with the low code development platforms market
  • Technical background dealing with development tools and the software development life cycle
  • Project management, release management and/or test management experience
  • Extra Bonus - Familiarity with LANSA and/or its main competitors
  • Extra Bonus - Familiarity with IBM technologies such as IBMi
  • Extra Bonus - Familiarity with Cloud Infrastructure

Location

This is a fully remote position offering a flexible work from home environment for candidates residing in Australia.

The role is open to contract arrangements only

jobs.title: Program Manager, Product & GTM Enablement
jobs.jd_full:
Our mission at Greenhouse is to make hiring work for everyone – so we go to great lengths to hire great people because we believe that they’re the foundation of our success. At Greenhouse, you’ll join a team that collaborates purposefully, fosters inclusivity, and communicates with transparency and accountability so we can achieve our mission.

Join us to do the best work of your career, solving meaningful problems with remarkable teams.

Greenhouse is looking for a Program Manager, Product + GTM Enablementto join our team!

This Program Manager will build and scale the enablement programs that help our Sales and Customer Success teams sell and support a fast-evolving product portfolio. This role owns the operational and curriculum backbone of GTM Enablement: turning product launches into repeatable training, managing the logistics and communications behind every rollout, and building the systems that let enablement scale across multiple audiences.

You’ll partner closely with Product Marketing, Product, Sales, Customer Success, and RevOps, and work directly with the leader of the Product + GTM Enablement team. This role is a strong fit for an organized, AI-fluent learning designer who turns ambiguity into training sellers can act on, and is able to own enablement programs end-to-end.

Who will love this job

  • A structured operator - You bring order and organization to fast-moving launches: rosters, timelines, trackers, content, comms, and collaboration.
  • A strong curriculum designer - You can take a product release and turn it into clear, reusable enablement, training, and job aids that change what reps do in the field.
  • A cross-functional collaborator - You’re comfortable coordinating PMM, Product, Sales, CS, and RevOps, and you move work forward without formal authority.
  • An AI adopter - You look for practical ways to use AI tools such as Glean, Claude, and more to automate manual work and free up time for what needs a human.
  • A biased-for-action doer- You move fast, ship, and iterate in a dynamic environment rather than waiting for perfection
  • A measurement-minded teammate - You care whether training actually landed, and you’ll track completion, sentiment, and behavior to prove it.

What you’ll do

  • Build and maintain product curriculum: eLearning, live sessions, job aids, playbooks, and FAQs for product launches and ongoing releases.
  • Own launch execution for GTM initiatives: timelines, session logistics, communications, invites, and follow-ups.
  • Maintain the systems that support enablement: tracking, reporting, scorecards, and AI knowledge agents, including turning the outputs into insights for stakeholders.
  • Partner on measurement: completion, sentiment, and behavior-change signals to demonstrate enablement impact.
  • Additional projects and responsibilities as business needs require.

You should have

  • 3–5 years of experience in enablement, program/project management, sales enablement, or a related GTM operations role in tech.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with a track record of running multiple launches or programs at once.
  • Instructional design experience, you’ve built training, job aids, or curriculum that people actually used. Direct GTM experience preferred.
  • Strong writing skills, with the ability to translate product briefs into concise, field-ready language.
  • Proficient with enablement tech stacks (LMS, conversation intelligence, CRM) and comfortable using AI tools in day-to-day work.
  • A data-informed mindset, using completion and feedback data to prioritize work and improve programs.
  • Familiarity with AI-powered tools and good judgment about when to automate versus when human decision-making matters most.
  • Experience in recruiting or B2B SaaS industry, a plus.
  • Your own unique talents! Your background has given you a unique perspective and set of transferable skills that aren’t always in alignment with a given role - but those are qualities we value at Greenhouse. If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications outlined above, we still strongly encourage you to apply

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.

If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents linked here .

The national pay range for this role is $88,100 - $101,960. Individual compensation will be commensurate with the candidate’s experience and qualifications. Certain roles may be eligible for additional compensation, including stock option awards, bonuses, and merit increases. Additionally, certain roles have the opportunity to receive sales commissions that are based on the terms of the sales commission plan applicable to the role.

Greenhouse provides a variety of benefits to employees, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, basic life insurance, mental health resources, financial wellness benefits, and a fully paid parental leave program. For US-based employees, we offer short-term and long-term disability coverage, a 401(k) plan and company match. U.S. based employees also receive, per calendar year, up to 14 scheduled paid holidays and up to 80 hours of paid sick leave. Non-exempt employees accrue up to 20-25 days of paid vacation time annually, depending on tenure, and exempt employees have flexible paid time off (PTO).

The anticipated closing date for this role is October 15, 2026.

Who we are

At Greenhouse, we live by our mission through using our own product to help us hire the right person for the job, every time. We’re committed to designing and responsibly using AI tools to transform how we work while keeping people at the center. We are a remote-first company and have shared office spaces in New York City and Ireland, and optional co-working spaces that give us flexibility to do our best work anywhere. We take an active role in our growth through a performance review program that’s committed to providing actionable feedback, and a bonus structure that rewards great performance. We believe that bringing together a variety of perspectives makes us a stronger company – and we nurture leaders who create an inclusive culture and invest into employee resource groups that celebrate our differences and life experiences. We’re proud to have built an award-winning culture that’s been recognized as Fortune’s Best Places to Work and Inc.’s Best Workplaces multiple years in a row.

jobs.title: Project Manager (Northeast)
jobs.jd_full:
GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation’s top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

General Description:

As a GuidePoint Security Project Manager, you are managing a unique portfolio of security focused Professional Services engagements which directly contribute to our client’s goals and success. This position may also require serving as a client-side billable resource for Project Management service delivery.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Efficient and effective management of Professional Services projects through the full engagement lifecycle:

    • Sales handoff

    • Resourcing

    • Customer project plan development

    • Execution management

    • Project closeout activities

  • Ensure regular and timely communications to all key stakeholders.

  • Manage project issues and risks to resolution.

  • Maintain and foster internal and external customer relationships, ensuring objectives and statement of work deliverables are met.

  • Plan and manage resources ensuring all projects meet scope and budget expectations.

  • Maintain the OpenAir PSA application for project data.

  • Manage and support internal processes for revenue recognition and customer invoicing.

  • Create and maintain project management methodology and process documentation.

  • Provide Project Management services to GuidePoint customers in a professional service capacity.

  • Other duties as assigned.

  • Adhere to GuidePoint Security Core Values.

Required Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent experience.

  • 3+ years of project management experience, including 2+ years in consulting services or a similar IT project management environment.

  • Experience with Agile methodology and project management tools such as Microsoft Project, Jira, OpenAir, Salesforce, or similar professional services applications.

  • Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel for project reporting.

  • Strong project management skills, including scope, scheduling, resources, budgets, timelines, and financial management.

  • Ability to manage multiple projects and teams simultaneously while maintaining customer satisfaction and project profitability.

  • Experience working with information security teams and understanding of key cybersecurity concepts and disciplines.

  • Understanding of professional services revenue recognition and invoicing.

  • Demonstrated leadership, mentoring, and team development experience.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively across technical and executive audiences.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, prioritization, and multitasking skills.

  • Ability to build strong customer relationships and drive successful project outcomes.

  • Experience with remote collaboration/teleconferencing tools and willingness to learn and use AI-enabled tools.

  • Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends as needed.

Preferred Experience:

  • Standard industry certifications.

  • Advanced computer skills with Mac and Google application experience.

Travel Requirements:

  • Willingness to travel up to 15%.

Physical Requirements:

  • Sedentary work.

  • Substantial movement of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers for a minimum of 8 hours a day.

  • Required to have close visual acuity to view computer terminal and/or extensive reading.

jobs.title: Senior Behavioral Health Program Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Description

Our Vision & Mission

We envision a world in which all people have access to high-quality and enduring solutions to improve and maintain their health and well-being. MCD Global Health aspires to be a premier partner of choice and a recognized leader, innovator, and trusted partner in healthcare and public health program development, implementation and evaluation. Our mission is to improve the health and well-being of people worldwide through enduring, high-quality, cost-effective, and universally accessible public health solutions. MCD operates impactful programs both in the U.S.A. and internationally.

MCD Global Health, Inc., in collaboration with the New England Rural Health Association (NERHA), is accepting applications for a Senior Behavioral Health Program Manager. The Senior Behavioral Health Program Manager works collaboratively with the Executive Director, Chief Operating Officer, association staff, and the NERHA Board of Directors to serve diverse members across the six-state region. This pivotal leadership role is responsible for the strategic oversight, execution, and management of several key rural health programs, primarily the Rural Opioid Technical Assistance Center (ROTA). The Senior Behavioral Health Program Manager provides direct supervision and mentorship to program staff and serves as a high-level external Behavioral Health liaison for the Association.

This is a full-time, exempt, remote/home-office position, and the successful candidate must live in New England. The position requires regular travel across the six New England states for regional meetings, site visits, and conferences, with occasional national travel.

This position is grant-funded, primarily supporting the Rural Opioid Technical Assistance Center (ROTA), and includes oversight of funding agreements and federal/state grants. The current grant runs through September 29, 2029.

Salary offers may be higher or lower than the anticipated salary listed due to various factors, including the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience.

Requirements

Senior Behavioral Health Program Manager – New England Rural Health Association (NERHA)

Anticipated Salary: $75,000 - $85,000

List of Job Duties:

The Senior Program Manager will support NERHA leadership, projects, and programs by performing/assisting with the following duties:

Program Oversight & Strategic Management

  • Program Leadership: Provide comprehensive project management and strategic direction for the ROTA project and other assigned rural health initiatives.

  • Provide Technical Assistance: Conduct direct behavioral health and substance use disorder TA to rural organizations

  • Subject Matter Expertise: Serve as the lead NERHA SME for Behavioral Health and SUD/OUD. Oversee development of trainings and resources providing rural and behavioral health expertise and insight

  • Partnership Coordination: Lead regular alignment meetings with the lead grant organization and key regional stakeholders to ensure all project planning and deliverables are met. Co-lead program advisory committee.

  • Grant & Compliance Management: Oversee the tracking, completion, and submission of all progress reports, data collections, and required documentation for funding agreements and federal/state grants. Assist in or lead development of appropriate grant proposals.

  • Workforce Development: Design and manage interprofessional, community-based internship and clerkship programs for students contributing to NERHA initiatives.

Staff Leadership & Personnel Management

  • Team Supervision: Directly manage, mentor, and evaluate program staff, coordinators, and interns, fostering a collaborative and high-performing team environment.

  • Resource Allocation: Delegate tasks effectively across programs and staff to optimize workflow, ensuring milestones are achieved on time and within budget.

Outreach, Engagement & Communications

  • TTA Recruitment: Develop recruitment plan for training and technical assistance, recruit participants from rural critical access hospitals, rural health clinics, Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), and community mental health centers.

  • Community Cultivation: Facilitate deep outreach and engagement within the NERHA network, identifying and supporting underrepresented and vulnerable rural communities across New England.

  • Leadership Engagement: Interface effectively and knowledgeably with executive leadership in rural organizations about the ROTA program and NERHA more broadly.

  • Conference Integration: Lead the development of program-specific events, including integrating specialized content and in-person components into the annual NERHA Rural Health Conference.

  • Strategic Communications: Develop and implement a comprehensive outreach and communication strategy to engage the NERHA network, including promotion, marketing, newsletters, training resources, and digital campaigns.

  • Project Evaluation & Reporting: Measure project performance to identify areas for improvement, monitor progress towards deliverables, and complete reports to the lead grant organization.

Other duties as assigned by the Executive Director or Chief Operating Officer

Qualifications & Experience

Required

  • Education: Masters Degree in Clinical Behavioral Health, Public Health, or a related field required

  • A minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in grant-funded program management, with at least 2 years directly supervising and mentoring clinical and program staff;

  • Extensive experience working to integrate clinical and community-based wraparound services to address social determinants of health needs in rural communities;

  • Excellent attention to detail;

  • Excellent written and oral communications skills;

  • Strong budget development, expense tracking, and financial monitoring skills

  • Proficiency with computers and Microsoft Office suite (e.g., Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project), cloud-based document management systems (e.g., Google Suite, One Drive, etc.), and with project management software tools, methodologies, and best practices;

  • Experience with contract and/or grants management and administration;

  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively, efficiently, and collaboratively in a fully remote or virtual environment.

Desirable

  • Clinical Behavioral Health Licensure (Licensed Clinical Professional Counselor, Licensed Clinical Social Worker) is highly desirable;

  • Deep familiarity with, commitment to, and/or personal experience living and working in rural communities;

  • Knowledge of/ experience with rural healthcare policy and networks;

  • Experience with community partners at the county/municipal/local level such as housing providers, transportation providers, law enforcement, food shelves, etc.

  • Live in and experience in New England.

Location and work environment

  • Status: Full-Time (Exempt), Regular Staff Position.

  • Schedule: Monday – Friday, standard business hours (with flexibility for evening or weekend events as required).

  • Location: Remote / Home Office.

  • Travel: Ability to travel regularly across the six New England states for regional meetings, site visits, and conferences, with occasional national travel.

  • Compensation: Competitive salary $75-85,000 commensurate with experience, plus a comprehensive benefits package (health, retirement, and paid time off).

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Here at Ooma we empower people to connect in smarter ways. We do this by creating powerful communication experiences through our cloud-based platform to bring people together at work and at home. Our solutions help small business owners stay connected with their customers and manage their businesses from anywhere. For larger companies we provide customized unified communications solutions to meet their unique needs. At home, we help our customers connect with their loved ones by providing the #1 rated VoIP phone service available. We also provide them with peace of mind through our innovative smart home security solution. At Ooma, all our products and services are priced competitively, because we believe advanced technology should be accessible to all.

About the Role:

We are seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead complex programs across our communications platforms, cloud infrastructure, applications, and operational systems. This role works closely with Engineering, Product, QA, Network Operations, DevOps/SRE, Security, Support, and business teams to take initiatives from requirements and technical planning through production deployment and operational readiness.

The ideal candidate is technically curious, highly organized, and comfortable working directly with engineers. This is not primarily a status-reporting role. The TPM is expected to understand the systems and dependencies well enough to identify problems, drive decisions, remove obstacles, and independently move programs forward.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own complex programs across VoIP/UCaaS/CCaaS platforms, cloud services, customer-facing applications, APIs, infrastructure, and operational systems from planning through production.
  • Translate product, customer, and engineering objectives into clear plans, milestones, owners, dependencies, and measurable outcomes.
  • Coordinate execution across Engineering, Product, QA, Network Operations, DevOps/SRE, Security, Support, and other teams.
  • Develop enough technical understanding of the systems being managed to effectively work with engineers, challenge assumptions, identify gaps, and drive issues to resolution.
  • Manage platform upgrades, software releases, infrastructure migrations, customer deployments, integrations, and reliability/performance initiatives.
  • Identify technical and organizational dependencies, risks, and bottlenecks early and drive mitigation or escalation.
  • Track execution rigorously and ensure commitments have clear owners and are driven through completion.
  • Communicate status, risks, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly to engineering leaders and executives.
  • Use operational and engineering metrics to improve delivery predictability, quality, reliability, and efficiency.
  • Continuously improve program-management processes and use automation and AI tools to reduce manual coordination and increase organizational leverage.
  • Operate effectively across globally distributed engineering teams and influence teams without direct reporting authority.

Experience We’re Looking For:

  • 8+ years of experience in technical program management, engineering program management, software or product development, or a closely related technical role.
  • Demonstrated success independently driving technically complex, cross-functional programs involving multiple engineering teams.
  • Strong understanding of software development lifecycles, APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, databases, networking, and production operations.
  • Ability and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies deeply enough to understand their architecture, dependencies, failure modes, and engineering tradeoffs.
  • Experience managing releases, migrations, integrations, production deployments, technical dependencies, risks, and competing priorities.
  • Strong organizational skills, with a demonstrated ability to create structure and execution discipline in ambiguous environments.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with engineers and senior leadership.
  • Experience with Jira, Confluence, dashboards and reporting tools, and modern AI-assisted productivity tools.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical technical experience.
  • Experience with VoIP/SIP, telecommunications, UCaaS/CCaaS, cloud communications, AWS, Azure, OCI, Linux, networking, carrier integrations, or related technologies is highly valued.
  • Prior experience in software engineering, systems engineering, QA automation, DevOps/SRE, solution architecture, or another hands-on technical discipline is a plus.
  • PMP, PgMP, Scrum, SAFe, or a similar certification is a plus, along with demonstrated technical expertise, strong ownership, and a proven track record of delivering complex programs.

What We Offer:

Working at Ooma means being a team player, while allowing your individual voice to come through. And,you’ll receive competitive compensation, benefits and generous company perks.

  • Comprehensive Medical/Dental/Vision insurance for you and eligible dependents
    • HMO, PPO’s or a PPO with a HDHP (including HSA, which Ooma helps fund)
  • Employer Paid Income Protection Benefits (Basic Life and AD&D, Short- and Long-term disability)
  • FSA Healthcare & Dependent Care
  • Commuter Benefits
  • Voluntary Accident, Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity and Legal
  • 401(k), including employer match, and Roth
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
  • Paid Time off, Sick Time, as well as corporate holidays observed
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Life Balance benefits with Travel Assistance Services and Identity Theft

We do not discriminate on the basis of any trait or characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

jobs.title: Project Manager, Activation - Operations Manager (Remote - Mexico Only)
jobs.jd_full:
Position Overview

Blue Acorn iCi is seeking a Project Manager, Activation (Operations Manager) to serve as the operational anchor of the Factory Migration Team — the day-to-day liaison between onshore program leadership and the offshore resources executing campaign and QA work. This role translates priorities downstream and surfaces status, risks, and blockers upstream in real time.

This is a hands-on-keyboard role, not a purely managerial one. Alongside directing the team, you will personally build, launch, and optimize campaigns and journeys in Adobe Journey Optimizer (AJO) as part of a migration from Oracle Eloqua onto the Adobe stack (AEP / RT-CDP B2B / AJO / CJA) — designing for the target state under a “rebuild, not export-import” strategy, not replicating legacy programs.

Location: Remote – Mexico only

Key Responsibilities

Onshore–Offshore Liaison

  • Serve as the operational point of contact between onshore leadership and offshore campaign/QA resources; translate priorities into clear work packages and return status, risks, and blockers before they become escalations.
  • Run the daily delivery rhythm — standups, cross-time-zone handoffs, and WIP tracking — and manage campaign-request intake: qualify, prioritize, assign, and track against SLAs.
  • Represent the Factory Migration Team in weekly Portfolio Reviews with the Studio.

Hands-On AJO Campaign Creation & Optimization

  • Build and configure B2B campaigns and journeys in AJO — triggers, events, decisioning, audiences, templates, and personalization — with consent, suppression, and frequency rules applied to every launch.
  • Execute campaign rebuilds through the Eloqua-to-Adobe migration: pilot, parallel run, phased waves, and cutover support.
  • Monitor in-flight performance and run structured optimization cycles (content, timing, audience, channel mix); partner with the CJA Specialist to ground decisions in data and feed findings back into playbooks and templates.

Team & Operations Management

  • Direct the day-to-day work of offshore Campaign Specialists and QA: assignments, workload balancing, quality expectations, and timelines.
  • Enforce the golden-path delivery workflow — standardized briefs, build checklists, QA gates, and launch approvals — and own launch quality: no campaign goes live without passing QA.
  • Track and report SLA, throughput, and quality metrics; maintain runbooks and SOPs; ramp new Factory resources as the team scales into 2027.

Collaboration

  • Partner with the Journey (AJO) Product Lead on standards and escalation of complex orchestration, the CDP Manager on audiences and activation, the CJA Specialist on measurement, and the QA Specialist on launch readiness.
  • Support UAT, deliverable acceptance, and production hypercare alongside onshore leads; validate compliance rules (TCPA, CAN-SPAM, GDPR) in campaign logic.

Required Skills & Experience

Experience

  • 5+ years in marketing operations, campaign management, or MarTech delivery.
  • 2+ years hands-on with Adobe Journey Optimizer building and launching production campaigns.
  • Experience leading or coordinating distributed delivery teams across time zones; prior agency or client-facing enterprise delivery experience.

Platform & Delivery Expertise

  • AJO — campaign/journey configuration, audiences, content, decisioning, and channel setup.
  • AEP / RT-CDP B2B working knowledge — profiles, segments, and datasets feeding journey logic; familiarity with CJA for measurement.
  • Email production fundamentals — templates, dynamic content, rendering, deliverability; Eloqua experience a strong plus given the migration.
  • Campaign delivery operations — intake and SLA management, QA discipline, runbooks/SOPs, and delivery metrics reporting.

Preferred Qualifications/Education

  • Fluent English (written and spoken) for daily work with US leadership and stakeholders; Spanish fluency for regional coordination.
  • Strong upward communication — concise status, early risk flagging, no-surprises escalation — and comfort holding a distributed team to quality and deadline standards.
  • Ability to align working hours to US Central/Eastern business hours, with flexibility to bridge offshore handoffs.
  • Ability to accommodate occasional travel for program milestones.
